intent: "Show me the actual calendar" — day by day, for a campaign or one person's participation, including what a weekend, a holiday, a closed window or a deferral moved.

per_item_results.detail: when a collection of enrolments is given.

input_schema.title: schedule.list input
input_schema.description: One page of the provider's named sending schedules, each with its windows as authored.

limit.description: At most this many schedules on the page. Required: absence is not a default, and a page may come back shorter.

offset.description: Where the page starts in the order `vendor.ordering` names: 0 for the first page, then the previous page's `offset` plus the number of items it returned.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it. The list names no campaign: a schedule is the team's, and any campaign may run on it.

external_id.description: The provider's identifier for the schedule, written as a string. Reported, never pinned.

name.description: The schedule's name, or null when the provider holds none.

time_zone.description: The time zone the windows are read in, as the provider spells it under its scheme, never converted: one zone of one scheme can be several of the other.

id.description: The provider's own spelling of the zone under `scheme`.

scheme.description: Which naming `id` is in: `iana`, the IANA time zone database's (`America/New_York`), or `windows`, the Windows time zone identifiers' (`Eastern Standard Time`).

in_recipient_time_zone.description: Whether the provider reads the windows in each person's own time zone, where it knows one, rather than in `time_zone`.

skips_holidays.description: Whether the provider sends nothing on the holidays of the calendars linked to the schedule. The calendars themselves are not listed.

default.description: Whether the schedule is the default of the user the plugin signs in as: the one that user's new campaigns start with.

follow_up_windows.description: The windows the campaign's later steps send in, where the provider keeps a second set of windows for them, or null where the schedule's own `windows` serve every step.

vendor.description: The provider's own word for the schedule's state, which publishes no vocabulary for it. A closed list, so nothing else travels here.

has_more.description: Whether the provider holds more schedules after this page.

ordering.description: The order `offset` counts in: by the provider's identifier, the lowest first, so a page asked for again starts where it did.

week.description: The windows by weekday, as authored: each weekday the provider holds, at most once, in the provider's own order. A weekday the provider holds nothing for is absent.

active.description: Whether the provider sends on this weekday at all.

ranges.description: The windows of the day, from and to, in the schedule's time zone.

time.description: A time of day, `HH:MM` on a 24-hour clock.

end.description: Where a window ends: a time of day, `HH:MM` on a 24-hour clock, or `24:00`, which is the end of that same day and never where a window starts.

failure_codes.when: The provider account's plan or the role of the user the plugin signs in as does not include its schedules.
The provider's answer was larger than this installation lets a plugin read from a program (`Plugins:Exec:OutputBytes`), so it was cut off; asking again would cut it the same way.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing could be listed. Repeating it runs the same call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it read this account's schedules.
The provider refused the read for now and it may be asked again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side.
The provider was called and no answer arrived. A read changes nothing and costs nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

The provider refused this call for a reason outside the work item — the account's money or plan, an allowance it counts, a credential it no longer accepts, a channel disconnected or paused — and did nothing for it. The failure's block says what is blocked, why and where a person clears it; a repeat once it clears is a first act. It is said even where the operation also declares an older code for the condition, which then stands for an answer the plugin cannot read as a block.

conformance: Every schedule the provider lists for the account is listed, except one the provider names no time zone for: the read takes no filter.

A page holds at most `limit` schedules, starting at `offset`, by the provider's identifier with the lowest first, and `has_more` says whether more follow; the next page starts at `offset` plus the number of items this page returned.
A page may come back short of `limit` with `has_more: true`: the plugin stops before the result would pass 768 KiB, counted as the runtime counts it.

The windows are the provider's as authored, by weekday, in the time zone the provider names, spelled as the provider spells it under the scheme that spelling belongs to; nothing is converted and no calendar is resolved.
A weekday the provider holds nothing for is absent, never invented as inactive.
`follow_up_windows` is null unless the provider keeps a second set of windows for the later steps and says it is in use.
A name the provider holds as empty is null, never an empty string.
A read pins nothing: the identifiers it lists are reported, never recorded by this one.
